data.current_summary: Full visa record, paid per request over x402 (no account, no API key)
data.current_description:
Same record as `GET /api/v1/visa` on a Pro plan, but paid per call over the
x402 protocol instead of an API key: 0.03 USD in USDC on Base.

Call it once without payment and it answers **402** with a
`PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header describing the offer; an x402 client signs a
`TransferWithAuthorization` (EIP-3009) and repeats the call. The payer needs
USDC but no ETH — the facilitator submits the transaction and pays the gas.

Settlement happens only after the handler returns a response below 400, so a
404 on an uncovered pair is never charged.

Free alternatives, if paying per call is not what you want:
`POST /api/v1/visa/register` for a free key, or the keyless MCP server at
<https://visa.orizn.app/mcp>.
data.summary_suggestion: Query full visa data with per-call USDC payment
data.description_suggestion: Returns the complete VisaData object (30 data points) for a passport-destination pair, payable per call in USDC on Base via x402 protocol. No account or API key required. Initial call returns 402 with payment offer; client signs EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization and repeats. Payer needs USDC only (no ETH required; facilitator covers gas). Settlement occurs only after successful response (< 400 status), so failed lookups are not charged. Equivalent to Pro plan `/api/v1/visa` endpoint but with micropayment billing instead of subscription quota.
data.reasoning: Original summary conflates technical protocol details with the actual operation purpose. Description is comprehensive but scattered across implementation details. Improved summary clarifies the action (query visa data) and payment model. Enhanced description leads with what the operation returns, then explains the payment flow and settlement mechanics, making it clearer for AI agents to understand when to use this versus the standard `/visa` endpoint.
